CHAMPION.Title: Champion's Legend
CHAMPION.HowTo: How it works at the table

protector.Name: Protector
protector.Desc: Stands up for the weak, defends people who have no one else.

slayer.Name: Slayer
slayer.Desc: Kills what others fear: beasts, monsters, foes in a fight to the death.

rebel.Name: Rebel
rebel.Desc: Does not kneel to lords. A hero to the commons, a threat to the nobility.

honorable.Name: Honourable
honorable.Desc: Keeps his word, fights fair, spares the defeated.

brute.Name: Brute
brute.Desc: Wins by breaking bones and finishing the fallen. Inspires fear, not respect.

rogue.Name: Rogue
rogue.Desc: Dirty tricks, sold fights, broken promises.

Legend.CircleTooltip: Bright and dark tales in the circle (total Weight)
Legend.RefuteHint: Gossip test at −10 per point of Weight. Success: the lie stops spreading.

Legend.Empty: Nobody tells stories about this champion yet. The first deed, petition or duel will change that.
Legend.HowTo:
A tale is a named deed that spreads among people. It has a face (who people think the champion is), a circle (who tells it) and a Weight: 1 Rumour (locality), 2 Tale (province), 3 Legend (the whole Empire).

Fame is the total Weight. Thresholds 3 / 7 / 12 / 18 give Tiers I–IV. The Tier says how easily a stranger recognises the champion (d10 ≤ 2 × Tier) and how often fame draws something in (Echo: d10 ≤ Tier + 1).

Invoking: once per session each tale can be invoked in a social test against someone who could have heard it. Bonus +1 SL per point of Weight. Bright tales support Charm, Leadership and Haggle, dark ones Intimidate.

Name: the player declares who he wants to be. The people name him after the face with the highest Weight. Calling the Name once per session gives 1 Resolve, and an accepted Name (people's face = declared, Weight ≥ 3) also 1 Fortune.

Petitions.Title: Petitions
Petitions.PromisesHint: The champion can promise help in at most three matters at a time.
Petitions.Empty: Nobody has come with a petition yet. The Echo of Fame or the GM will change that. Drag an actor here to add a petitioner.
Petitions.TooMany: The champion already has three promises.
Petitions.DeclineHint: Declining a serious or life-and-death matter dims the legend in the petitioner's circle.
Petitions.StakeHint: Stake: the Weight of the tale that will be born (or the bad fame if he fails).
Petitions.HowTo:
People come to the champion with petitions. The player chooses which to promise help with (at most 3 promises at a time).

  • Fulfilled: a tale is born with Weight equal to the stake, in the petitioner's circle.
  • Failed: a "he broke his word" tale is born with the Rogue face and the same Weight.
  • Declined: no cost for a small matter. For a serious or life-and-death matter the strongest bright tale in that circle loses 1 Weight.

Petitions are ready adventure hooks for the whole party.

Arena.NoDuelText: A duel is a scene in four acts: challenge, seconds, a fight before the crowd and the aftermath. Drag an actor here or pick a rival.
Arena.RivalEdgesHint: The GM decides how many dirty advantages the rival has (poison, a bribed judge, his own scout). Each rival edge is +1 SL to one of his tests.
Arena.PlayToCrowdHint: An Action in combat: Charm test. Success: Crowd +1 (SL ≥ 3: +2). Failure by 3+ SL: Crowd −1.

Edge.weakness: Rival's weakness (+2 SL to one test against him)

Arena.NoEdges: No edges. The scout can find some during preparations.
Arena.DirtyHint: Sand in the eyes, a low blow: Crowd −1, and the tale of a victory will have the Rogue face.
Arena.LinkCombatHint: With Crowd ≥ +2 the champion gains +1 Advantage at the start of every round; at ≤ −2 the rival gains it.

StageHelp.challenge: Agree the terms, venue and stakes. The GM decides how many edges the rival has. Announce the challenge in chat.
StageHelp.prep: Every player can become a second and make one test. Successes give edges, betting odds, the crowd's favour and dressings.
StageHelp.fight: Fight with the normal WFRP rules. The crowd reacts to the fight and at ±2 gives one side Advantage each round.
StageHelp.aftermath: Who won, and what happened to the loser? That is where the tale is born.

scout.Name: Scout
scout.Effect: Asks around about the rival. Success: edge "Rival's weakness" (SL ≥ 3: two).

herald.Name: Herald
herald.Effect: Warms up the crowd. Success: the Crowd starts at +1 (SL ≥ 3: +2).
herald.Success: The crowd is on the champion's side ({crowd}).
herald.Failure: The crowd stays indifferent or hostile ({crowd}).

bookie.Name: Bookie
bookie.Effect: Bets on the fight. Success: odds 2:1 (SL ≥ 3: 3:1). Failure: 1:1.

armsman.Name: Squire
armsman.Effect: Checks weapons and judges. Success: cancels one rival edge (SL ≥ 3: two).

surgeon.Name: Surgeon
surgeon.Effect: Prepares dressings. Success: after the fight the champion regains 1 + SL Wounds.

Mood.-3: The crowd whistles and throws mud
Mood.2: The crowd chants the champion's name

Favour.none: The crowd gives no one Advantage yet

Arena.HowTo:
1. Challenge: terms (to first blood / until one yields / to the death), audience (1–3) and stakes. The GM sets the rival's edges.

2. Seconds: five roles (Scout, Herald, Bookie, Squire, Surgeon). Each is taken by another player or an NPC and makes one test. This way the whole party plays in the champion's scene.

3. Fight: normal WFRP combat. A champion's edge is +2 SL to one test against the rival. Crowd from −3 to +3: at ±2 the side it supports gains +1 Advantage at the start of every round. Playing to the crowd is a Charm test instead of an Action.

4. Aftermath: a victory births a tale with Weight = audience (+1 with Crowd ≥ 2, −1 at ≤ −2). The face depends on what the champion does with the loser: spares him (Honourable), humiliates him (Rebel against the mighty, Brute against the weaker) or kills him (Slayer in a fight to the death, Brute against the terms). A dirty trick turns the face into Rogue. A defeat dims the legend unless the crowd was for the champion.

Rivals.Title: Rivals
Rivals.RecordHint: The champion's wins – losses – draws against this rival
Rivals.Empty: No rivals. Every defeated foe and every challenger from the Echo of Fame lands here. Drag an actor here.
Rivals.HowTo:
Rivals remember. A spared rival becomes a debtor (grudge −1), a humiliated one swears revenge (grudge +2), a killed one is gone, but his kin may come back. A draw is grudge +1.

When the Echo of Fame rolls a challenger, the rival with the greatest grudge returns first.
